title: Silas and the Deadline
premise: Coral Ishikawa, a financial-crimes investigator who launders reputations as much as money, is handed an impossible case: a passenger flight whose booking records, manifests, and payment trails have been erased mid-flight, leaving a plane full of people who officially never boarded. Digging in, Coral discovers the erasure was bought by Meridian Trust — the quiet firm that has been cleaning Coral's own fabricated identity for years — and that the flight carries a whistleblower holding proof of a global laundering network. To save the passengers and themselves, Coral must trade the one secret worth killing for: the original documents proving who they really were before Meridian rebuilt them. In the end, Coral burns their false history to expose the network, loses the family that made them, and gains a truer one among the survivors.
about_author: Bram Amberdale spent a decade in compliance offices across three continents before turning to fiction, writing at kitchen tables in port cities where money changes accents. They are known for thrillers in which paperwork is more dangerous than gunfire.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A routine day scrubbing an ugly client's ledger establishes Coral's world: invisible work, unattributable credit, and the found-family of misfits at the firm. The emotional beat is weary competence masking loneliness; Coral is good at making things disappear, including themselves.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. An alert pings: flight 447's bookings, manifests, and payment records vanish while the plane is still airborne. Coral confirms it isn't a glitch — someone paid to erase three hundred people in real time. Beat: cold dread blooming into obsessive curiosity.

chapters.title: Nobody Boarded
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On the tarmac, officials insist no such flight exists; passengers' families get silence. Coral interviews a gate agent whose memory of boarding is the only surviving record. Beat: the horror of institutional gaslighting, and Coral's first taste of being believed by no one.

chapters.title: Meridian Trust
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Tracing the erasure fee leads to Meridian Trust, the discreet firm that once manufactured Coral's new identity after they fled their old life. Realizing their protector may be the enemy, Coral hides the lead from colleagues. Beat: betrayal and self-preservation war.

chapters.title: The Passenger List That Isn't
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Dana Okafor, an off-duty journalist aboard 447, notices the cabin crew acting strange and starts photographing everything. Her chapter reveals a nervous man clutching an encrypted drive. Beat: claustrophobic suspense; the erased are awake inside their own erasure.

chapters.title: Old Names
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral visits the forger who built their identity, finding her terrified and packing to run. She warns that Meridian doesn't erase companies — it erases witnesses. Beat: fear curdling into resolve; Coral understands they were always on a list.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. The nervous man slips the encrypted drive into Dana's seat pocket before being escorted off the plane at a refueling stop — and doesn't reboard. Beat: guilt and adrenaline; Dana now holds something she can't name and can't return.

chapters.title: Attribution Problem
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral's boss orders the flight file closed and sealed — someone above is leaning down. Coral copies the file anyway, crossing a line from investigator to target. Beat: quiet insubordination; the found family at the office begins to fracture under pressure.

chapters.title: The Drive
chapters.summary: Dana's POV, landing abroad. Dana cracks partial encryption: the drive maps a laundering lattice touching banks, charities, and governments — with Meridian at its center. Beat: vertigo of scale; she realizes why three hundred people had to become nobody.

chapters.title: Two Strangers
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Coral, following the drive's signature, finds Dana's hotel. Mutual suspicion gives way to alliance over bad coffee and matching paranoia. Beat: wary connection — two people defined by false or stolen identities recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What Coral Was Before
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Flashback woven through present: the crime, the flight from home, the deal with Meridian that purchased a new name. Now Coral realizes Meridian kept the originals as leverage. Beat: shame transformed into strategy — the secret is also a weapon.

chapters.title: Sealed Cabin
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. News breaks that 447's remaining passengers are being 'relocated' by a private security contractor. Dana recognizes the contractor's funding pattern from the drive. Beat: ticking clock engaged; the erased are being tidied away permanently.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Meridian's fixer, Voss, makes contact: hand over the drive and Coral's original identity documents stay buried, plus a generous retirement. Coral stalls, buying time while recording everything. Beat: temptation played straight — safety offered at the price of complicity.

chapters.title: Family Business
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral confesses everything to their closest colleague, Priya, expecting expulsion; instead Priya offers help, forming a three-person resistance. Beat: warmth against the cold — found family chosen deliberately at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Voss's team raids Dana's room; she escapes with the drive through a service corridor, wounded but free, guided by Coral over the phone. Beat: kinetic chase; trust tested and proven under fire.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Decrypted fully, the drive reveals Meridian's master ledger — including Coral's own entry, filed under 'assets, renewable.' Beat: devastating clarity; Coral sees exactly what they are to the people who saved them.

chapters.title: Flight Path
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The trio locates the hangar where 447's passengers are held pending 'disposition,' and plans extraction using Coral's laundering expertise to move people the way money moves: quietly, in structured batches. Beat: hope engineered from expertise.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, the only antagonist chapter. His pragmatism, his genuine belief he prevents chaos, his orders to erase everyone involved. Beat: chilling humanity; the reader sees the machine smiling.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, climax part one. At the exchange, Coral offers not the drive but the trade promised in the blurb: the original identity documents Meridian holds — surrendering their past publicly, live-streamed, so killing them proves nothing anymore. Beat: sacrificial gambit; the secret's value dies in daylight.

chapters.title: Hangar Nine
chapters.summary: Dual POV, climax part two. While Voss's attention is consumed by the broadcast, Priya and Dana spring the passengers; the ledger uploads to every regulator simultaneously. Voss falls not to violence but to exposure. Beat: catharsis through coordination, not firepower.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unattributed
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The network collapses; Coral's old name surfaces in the leaks, forcing reckoning with the person they were. Some colleagues walk away; Priya and Dana stay. Beat: grief and relief braided together; identity as ongoing choice, not document.

chapters.title: Boarding Pass
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, coda. Months later, Coral — working openly now, credited by name — helps the 447 survivors rebuild their paper lives, then boards a real flight under their real name for the first time. Beat: belonging earned; the door of the plane closing sounds like a beginning.
